In an extensive interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and its plans for a tab-less interface. Watch the video below.

ChatGPT may seamlessly support workflows

A few days ago, Joanna Stern released a trailer for her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern released the full interview, covering topics including the new ChatGPT voice feature, OpenAI's hardware development plans, the Apple lawsuit, and the recent Hugging Face hack.

During the interview, Stern mentioned OpenAI's recent decision to merge ChatGPT with the Codex desktop app, along with the launch of ChatGPT's new agent mode, "Work".

The merged interface caused confusion, especially for users who only wanted to continue using ChatGPT but found it hard to locate their chat history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, adding separate "Work" and "Chat" tabs at the top of the interface, and a dropdown menu on the left panel to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is now easier to navigate, it is still somewhat complicated.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern that the new interface was "a bit messy," and added that it represents "a stepping stone toward the future," where the "Work" tab will disappear and its functionality will "seamlessly blend into ChatGPT".

Brockman also said that, despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI still achieved its expected results, with Codex users growing from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether this growth was purely a result of bundling Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman acknowledged this again, while also arguing that this was partly the intent:

The full interview is rich in content and well worth watching. The interview also features a very Joanna Stern-style attempt at integrating the ChatGPT voice feature into the conversation, which goes about as smoothly as you might expect.
